reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "An Odd Venetian Deck Examined", "body": "Chance introduced the Sola Busca as one of the oddest tarot decks, sharing little with the modern tarot beyond its numbering. When he asked when it originated, the answer given was about 1490, and Chance called the artwork a serious commission. Mario said he believed the deck held many secrets that had never been discussed, and that anyone who studied it could still find new ones. The group worked through the trumps in order, with slides comparing each card to its Rider-Waite counterpart. One guest said he understood that only one complete early deck survives, so some odd details might be damage."}, {"title": "Philology and Priestly Wordplay", "body": "Dylan traced Taurus and its relatives in Greek, Latin and French to a shared root tied to height and rank. Across the evening, guests hunted through Latin and Greek for hidden meanings, treating card names, ribbons, spears, shields and flags as possible wordplay. One speaker, drawing on a book about Mesopotamian star lore, suggested that ancient priests prized several meanings in a single word. One guest cautioned that without the original names for each object, the group might be missing symbolism that would have been obvious to viewers of the time."}, {"title": "Sun Cycles and the Nero Question", "body": "One guest put forward the hypothesis that the deck might encode the Neros cycle and a lineage of messiah figures, while saying it would take much more work to prove. Several speakers read the card sequence as a calendar, with the sun turning hostile as autumn arrived and barren landscapes appearing on many cards. The panel also discussed Peter Mark Adams's view, relayed on air, that the deck was made with malefic intent and might encode methods of controlled reincarnation. The speaker relaying it said he was open to that idea if reincarnation was real."}, {"title": "Phoenician Purple and Mithraic Echoes", "body": "The group noticed Phoenician purple on nearly every card, which led one speaker to the murex shell dye and to the odd shell shapes on later cards. Dylan argued that under the Justinian code wearing Syrian purple would have been punishable unless the wearer was royal. One speaker suggested the Venetian merchant families behind the deck may have opposed the Vatican. Gabe argued that green, white and red on national flags showed the imprint of Mithraic orders, and said he would track down the researcher behind that claim and share it on Telegram."}, {"title": "Mario on Death, Orion, and Scorpio", "body": "At card thirteen Mario argued that the spear, shield and helmet formed a hidden scythe, which he tied to the Death card. He noted that other Death cards showed severed heads and suggested the oversized head here encoded Orion being stung by the Scorpion. He said it was the first card where he believed he had found something he had not read elsewhere. Peter Mark Adams's link between the card and the star Algol, the eye of Medusa, was relayed on air, and speakers also raised Cato the Elder and the constellation Ophiuchus."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: One of the biggest mysteries of the occult is the tarot, especially the fact that there is no "official" version. Mario Garza of Symbolic Studies and Dylan Saccoccio of the Spirit Whirled series join us tonight to decode the Sola Busca deck, one of the most ancient, and strangest, of all arcana. This is likely to be too big for one show, so if you enjoy it and want more, let us know!
